CHIEF COMPLAINT
Smoking cessation

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
44-year-old patient presents motivated to quit smoking. Patient began smoking in high school as experimentation with friends and at parties, which progressed to daily use. Currently smoking 1.5 packs per day with first cigarette within one hour of waking. Patient has one prior quit attempt using cold turkey method, during which he successfully abstained for almost one year before relapsing due to work-related stress from layoffs and increased responsibilities. Patient recently started meditation and joined a gym as stress management strategies. Patient is highly motivated to quit due to impending fatherhood (daughter expected any day). Patient is willing to use nicotine patch for smoking cessation. Quit date set for next Monday (patient's birthday).

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies use of other tobacco products. No other symptoms elicited.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Type 2 diabetes
2. Gout
3. Systolic heart murmur (2/6, previously noted)

MEDICATIONS
Allopurinol

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Employed. History of work-related stress from recent layoffs and increased job responsibilities. Recently joined gym and started meditation practice. Wife expecting first child (daughter) imminently.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vitals: BP 128/88, HR 68, RR 16, O2 sat 98% on room air
Heart: Regular rate and rhythm; 2/6 systolic murmur appreciated (known from prior exams)
Lungs: Clear and equal bilaterally; no expiratory wheezes; no rales or rhonchi
Neck: No lymphadenopathy; no carotid bruits appreciated

RESULTS
Hemoglobin A1c ordered for next blood draw

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Nicotine Dependence: Patient commended for taking first step toward smoking cessation. Starting 21 mg nicotine patch on Monday (quit date). Will taper dose over time with no fixed timeline. Patient instructed to change patch location daily to avoid skin irritation. Provided handout regarding common smoking triggers. Patient to continue exercise routine and implement stress management strategies including meditation and yoga. Particular attention to monitoring stress related to work and upcoming birth of child. Follow-up appointment in 2 weeks to assess progress and reevaluate nicotine patch dosage.

2. Type 2 Diabetes: Continue current management with diet and exercise. Monitor glucose control. Hemoglobin A1c to be drawn prior to next visit in 2 weeks and results will be reviewed at follow-up appointment.

3. Gout: Continue allopurinol. Patient counseled to continue monitoring foods that exacerbate uric acid levels. Follow-up in 2 weeks.
